agency_full: European Space Agency (Mercury Planetary Orbiter + Mercury Transfer Module) / Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, Mio)
payload: 4100 kg launch stack: MTM (Mercury Transfer Module, ESA — 4 ion thrusters, solar arrays) + MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter, ESA, 1230 kg, 11 instruments) + MIO (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, JAXA, 285 kg, 5 instruments) + MOSIF sunshield. Two science orbiters separate after Mercury arrival.
credit: © ESA / JAXA / Airbus. BepiColombo launched 2018-10-20 from Kourou — the joint Europe-Japan flagship to Mercury, named after Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo, the Italian mathematician who designed Mariner 10's multi-flyby trajectory. The 8-year cruise uses 9 gravity assists (Earth 2020-04-10, Venus 2020-10-15, Venus 2021-08-10, then six Mercury flybys 2021–2025) plus continuous ion-electric thrust from the Mercury Transfer Module to bleed off the enormous solar-gravity gradient between Earth and Mercury orbits. Mercury orbit insertion is set for 2026-11-21, with science operations beginning early 2027 after MTM jettison and MPO + Mio separation. Primary science: Mercury's exospheric composition + dynamics, the composition of its iron-rich crust and Caloris-class large impact basins, the structure of its magnetic field + magnetospheric tail, and tests of Einstein's general relativity via radio-science range tracking through Mercury's strong solar-gravity environment. Nominal one-year mission with one-year extension authorised.

events.label: Launch — Ariane 5 ECA
events.description: Kourou, French Guiana, 2018-10-20. Joint ESA / JAXA mission carrying two science orbiters — ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) + JAXA's Mio (formerly Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter) — stacked on a Mercury Transfer Module that uses electric propulsion + nine planetary flybys to lose enough energy to capture into Mercury orbit.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 12,700 km on 2020-04-10. The first of nine flybys needed to lose orbital energy and spiral inward toward Mercury. Reaching Mercury directly from Earth is among the hardest interplanetary transfers — the spacecraft's heliocentric velocity must DROP by ~25 km/s, the opposite of an outer-system mission's accelerate-and-go problem.

events.label: Venus #1 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 10,720 km on 2020-10-15. First of two Venus assists. Venus's gravity is used here to BRAKE the spacecraft — taking energy out of the heliocentric orbit so the perihelion drops toward Mercury's distance from the Sun.

events.label: Venus #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 552 km on 2021-08-10 — much closer than Venus #1. The deeper flyby drops aphelion further, setting up the first of six Mercury flybys 11 months later.

events.label: Mercury #1 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 199 km from Mercury's surface on 2021-10-01 — the first BepiColombo Mercury observation, four years before formal orbit insertion. Each successive Mercury flyby brakes the spacecraft further, shrinking its orbit closer to Mercury's.

events.label: Mercury #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 200 km on 2022-06-23. Cumulative ∆v from gravity assists exceeds 6 km/s by this pass — work the chemical engine + electric thrusters can't have done alone within the propellant budget.

events.label: Mercury #3 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 236 km on 2023-06-19. Mid-cruise checkpoint — instruments continue commissioning over the high-altitude legs.

events.label: Mercury #4 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 165 km on 2024-09-04. Closest flyby to date in the BepiColombo sequence; the proximity adds substantial braking ∆v.

events.label: Mercury #5 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach planned for 2024-12-01. Penultimate Mercury flyby — the final two assists shrink the orbit to the geometry required for capture.

events.label: Mercury #6 — gravity assist
events.description: Final flyby planned for 2025-01-08 — the spacecraft's orbital period matches Mercury's well enough that orbital capture is feasible at the next solar conjunction window.

events.label: Mercury orbit insertion + spacecraft separation
events.description: Planned 2026-11. The Mercury Transfer Module separates and the two orbiters (ESA MPO + JAXA Mio) split into their respective science orbits. MPO maps the surface geology + interior structure; Mio characterises Mercury's tenuous magnetosphere. First two-orbiter Mercury mission ever flown.
